name: credit-score
title: Credit Score
description: A credit score card whose number counts up while a bar meter lights from red through amber to green.

perf.budget: The meter lights bar by bar with UI-thread timings; the number counts up for about a second (re-rendering on animation frames).

measurements.notes: Janky frames come from the number counting up (a React re-render per frame for about a second).

a11y.reducedMotion: The score shows at once and the bars light without the left-to-right sweep.
a11y.screenReader: The score reads as one line with its band and scale ("Your credit score is 712, Good, on a scale of 300 to 850").
a11y.touchTarget: The header button is at least 44 pt.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { CreditScore } from '@/components/kinetik/credit-score';

<CreditScore
  score={report?.score ?? 0}
  icon={<GaugeIcon />}
  action={{ label: 'Apply', icon: <PlusIcon />, onPress: startApplication }}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Showing one score on a known scale, with room to say what to do when there is none.

## When not to use

- Scores without bands or a scale: the colours imply good and bad.
- Several scores side by side: use a chart.

## Notes

- `min` and `max` default to 300 and 850. A score below `min` (such as 0) shows the empty state and `emptyHint`.
- Bands are Poor, Fair, Good, Very good and Excellent by share of the scale; `scoreBand` is exported if you need the same words elsewhere.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add credit-score`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
